# Release identity and deployment commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs/release-alignment.mjs from package metadata and checked command names. -->

**Current software version: v1.19.3.** The root, Hardhat, UI and deployment registry must agree. Use one published release and its matching source, instructions and checksums. Historical release records, qualification reports and legal notices retain their original dates and versions.

| Component | Version | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public source | 1.19.3 | Root package and release manifest |
| Hardhat deployment workspace | 1.19.3 | hardhat/package.json and lockfile |
| UI workspace | 1.19.3 | ui/package.json and lockfile |
| Deployment registry | 1.19.3 | config/usdc-deployment.json; version labels software, not an on-chain deployment |

Check [release and download availability for v1.19.3](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.19.3). Published tags and release assets identify their exact source. Later main-branch changes and candidate builds require separate qualification; they do not inherit the release evidence. The [previous published release v1.19.2](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.19.2) remains available for historical comparison.

Checksums bind content; they do not establish GitHub-enforced immutability. Maintainers should [enable release immutability](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/establish-provenance-and-integrity/prevent-release-changes) before future releases and verify `immutable: true` in the published release metadata. Existing releases are not retroactively protected.

Merging runs website validation but does not publish Pages. After reviewing the applicable checks on the exact main revision, a maintainer must separately dispatch the GitHub Pages workflow with `publish: true` and `source_commit` equal to that revision's full SHA. A mismatched SHA stops the workflow. Release publication and intake activation remain separate decisions.

## Choose the creation route

For the owner-entered Ubuntu mainnet route, use the [hidden-prompt creator guide](deployment/ubuntu-ephemeral-creator.md). It takes the deployer key only through its local hidden prompt and rejects deployment dotenv files, secret environment values and secret arguments. Use a separate reviewed checkout without running the environment-backed setup below. The creator and Ledger governor are separate; governor configuration and activation remain separate actions.

## Prepare the environment-backed route

Use Node 22.23.2 for the public qualification/deployment workflow and the committed lockfiles. From the source root:

```bash
npm ci
npm --prefix hardhat ci
npm --prefix hardhat run setup
```

Review the generated private configuration and both settlement recipients, final owner, chain, native USDC and identity settings. See [the complete Hardhat procedure](../hardhat/README.md) and [every supported setting](DEPLOYMENT_CONFIGURATION.md). Private Fleet runtimes have their own Node requirements in their package guides.

## Commands from the source root

These command names are checked against the executable Hardhat package scripts. Plans explicitly select read-only mode; missing or empty DRY_RUN also defaults to read-only.

| Task | Command | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create private configuration | `npm --prefix hardhat run setup` | Offline; preserves existing files |
| Check mainnet profile | `npm --prefix hardhat run check:config:mainnet` | Offline; no signer or RPC |
| Check Sepolia profile | `npm --prefix hardhat run check:config:sepolia` | Offline; no signer or RPC |
| Compile pinned contracts | `npm --prefix hardhat run compile` | Local compiler; no chain transactions |
| Test preflight and recovery | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:preflight` | Local fixtures |
| Test compiler-derived registry | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:registry-native` | Pinned compiler and disposable local chain |
| Test actual local deployments | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:deployment` | Disposable local chain |
| Test historical native USDC | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:mainnet-fork` | Local fork; no public-chain broadcasts |
| Test USDC/ENS cutover | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:cutover` | Local fork; preserves historical evidence |
| Plan mainnet deployment | `DRY_RUN=1 npm --prefix hardhat run deploy:mainnet` | Explicit DRY_RUN=1; chain reads only |
| Plan Sepolia deployment | `DRY_RUN=1 npm --prefix hardhat run deploy:sepolia` | Explicit DRY_RUN=1; chain reads only |
| Plan mainnet ENS helper | `DRY_RUN=1 npm --prefix hardhat run deploy:ens-job-pages:mainnet` | Explicit DRY_RUN=1; chain reads only |
| Plan Sepolia ENS helper | `DRY_RUN=1 npm --prefix hardhat run deploy:ens-job-pages:sepolia` | Explicit DRY_RUN=1; chain reads only |
| Recover mainnet source verification | `npm --prefix hardhat run reverify:mainnet` | Chain reads and explorer requests; no chain broadcasts |
| Recover Sepolia source verification | `npm --prefix hardhat run reverify:sepolia` | Chain reads and explorer requests; no chain broadcasts |
| Recover existing review escrow on mainnet | `npm --prefix hardhat run recover:review-escrow:mainnet` | Read-only plan by default; existing address/journal required; no new deployment |
| Recover existing review escrow on Sepolia | `npm --prefix hardhat run recover:review-escrow:sepolia` | Read-only plan by default; existing address/journal required; no new deployment |
| Check mainnet instance | `npm --prefix hardhat run check:readiness` | Read-only; requires saved receipt and reviewed NFT policy |
| Check Sepolia instance | `npm --prefix hardhat run check:readiness:sepolia` | Read-only; requires saved receipt and reviewed NFT policy |

Manager verification recovery requires DEPLOYMENT_RECEIPT; existing review-escrow recovery instead requires REVIEW_ESCROW_ADDRESS and its original journal. Readiness additionally requires READINESS_NFT_CONFIG and, only for reviewed identity changes, READINESS_CONFIG. Relative environment paths use the Hardhat npm process directory; follow the configuration reference. A successful offline check does not validate a live instance.

## Authorize deployment and then intake separately

The environment-backed commands in this inventory require explicit DRY_RUN=0, the selected funded signer and explorer verification for actual deployment. Mainnet additionally requires DEPLOY_CONFIRM_MAINNET=I_UNDERSTAND_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT. The recommended [Ubuntu hidden-prompt route](deployment/ubuntu-ephemeral-creator.md) has its own public-plan confirmation and recovery procedure; it does not use those secret-bearing environment settings. Follow the selected route after reviewing its exact source and plan; this command inventory does not authorize a broadcast.

Current-schema creation assigns the explicit governor atomically and starts the manager paused. Verify owner() equals the reviewed governor and pendingOwner() is zero; no creator handover or ownership acceptance is required. Preserve the journal and exact compiler input, finish verification and pass the actual instance's [launch checklist](LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md). Historical six-argument deployment records retain their original two-step handover; later voluntary Manager ownership changes also remain two-step. A failed command may already have broadcast; inspect receipts before retrying. Optional ENS helper creation has its own journal and leaves governor configuration in a separate action plan.

## Qualification boundaries

| Evidence | What it establishes | Separate evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release CI | Behavior of the pinned source and tested scenarios | Independent review and the actual operator setup |
| Hardhat readiness | Recorded contract code, owner, token, recipients, selected policies and reserve state | Other mutable policies, signer security, monitoring and participant operations |
| Economic admission | Signed assumptions and configured cost/capital/capacity limits | Observed employer value, actual costs and independent participants |
| Private Fleet commissioning | Rehearsed execution on the operator's actual machines and services | Sustained useful throughput and ongoing recovery measurements |

The existing manager and its payout rules are unchanged. New work uses [no-retainer operations](OPERATIONS/NO_RETAINERS.md). Existing AGIReviewEscrow records are retained for credit and refund recovery. The companion escrow script permits only source-verification recovery against its original journal; new escrow deployment is disabled. Publishing software does not open intake, qualify private hardware or establish production throughput. Manual console posting does not enforce [pre-funding qualification](OPERATIONS/PREFUNDING.md).
